chapter: Learning, lawn parties and band rivalries
title: Rene Batiste and the violinist Ferdinand Valteau
summary: Dawson barely knew Rene Batiste and remembers old man Valteau as a good violinist who freelanced and never held a regular band job.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Like Richard Payne? Did you know Richard Payne? Or Joe Brooks? Or what's that Batiste call's name? Rene Batiste?
Rene, uh, uh, uh, uh, Kid Rene.
Well, Rene Batiste, that played with the Imperial, I think, huh?
Yeah, Batiste, yeah. I believe I heard of him, huh? I didn't know him much. You didn't know that? No, I didn't know much about him.
What about the old man Valto? Ferdinand Valto?
Valto, he was a violin player. Uh-huh. Yeah, he was a good old violin player.
Uh-huh. You don't know who he played with?

He played with no, I don't think he played with any, any band. He just played, uh, catch what he could, you know, different, different musicians would hire him, you know. He's a, extra fella. Yeah. He never played with no sturdy band to my knowing. I don't know.
Did you ever play on any serenades with him? No.
